chunks: From him, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'When the immoral woman is asked, "Who committed fornication with you?" and she says, "So-and-so," then upon her are two penalties: a penalty for her immorality, and a penalty for her accusation against the Muslim man.'

key_terms.الْفَاجِرَةُ: The immoral woman (specifically one subject to hadd)
key_terms.حَدَّيْنِ: Two penalties (legal punishments prescribed by Sharia)

ai.seo_question: What are the two penalties for an immoral woman who names her partner in fornication?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the principle of cumulative penalties in Shia jurisprudence, where the immoral woman (al-fajira) bears both the hadd for her own zina and the hadd for qadhf (slander) against the named man. Scholars note that this dual liability arises because her accusation is treated as a distinct legal offense separate from her personal sin, provided the man she names is a Muslim. This ruling underscores the precision of Islamic penal law in distinguishing between the act of fornication and the act of false testimony.
